problem:
The matrix $T$ is given below. Let ${t}_{1}$, ${t}_{2}$, and ${t}_{3}$ be the respective columns of $T.$
Determine if $B=\text{{}{t}_{1},{t}_{3}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(T).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${t}_{2}={x}_{1}{t}_{1}+{x}_{3}{t}_{3}.$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & -6\end{aligned}]
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Finding a Basis of the Column Space of a Matrix

feedback.problem:
The matrix $U$ is given below. Let ${u}_{1}$, ${u}_{2}$, and ${u}_{3}$ be the respective columns of $U.$
Determine if $B=\text{{}{u}_{1},{u}_{3}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(U).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${u}_{2}={x}_{1}{u}_{1}+{x}_{3}{u}_{3}.$

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 \\ -4 & 8 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $U$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}U & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 \\ -4 & 8 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(-\frac{1}{4}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $3$rd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(U)$ is ${{u}_{1},{u}_{3}},$ that is to say,

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 8\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Now, since the $2$nd column of the reduced matrix is a non-pivot column, then the entries in that column tell us the coefficients needed to express ${u}_{2}$ as a linear combination of all the other columns in the original matrix. So, we have

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 8\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{u}_{2}}={{(-2)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{u}_{1}}+{{(0)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{3}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 8\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{u}_{3}}.
$$

This gives us ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}=(-2)\cdot 0=0.$
